controls.title: Cryptographic inventory
controls.objective: A maintained inventory records algorithms, key sizes, protocols, libraries, certificates, and owners for each system, including vendor products.

evidence.description: Sample scan of TLS endpoints and code dependencies

questions.text: Which best describes the cryptographic inventory?

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Certificates or TLS endpoints listed, but algorithms, libraries, and owners are not recorded.

anchors.label: System level
anchors.description: Every critical system lists its algorithms, key sizes, protocols, libraries, and owner.

anchors.label: Complete
anchors.description: System-level inventory also covers vendor products, embedded and OT devices, and is updated at least every 6 months.

questions.guidance: Ask for the inventory and check 3 systems against a scan.

questions.text: Percentage of critical systems with algorithms and key sizes recorded in the inventory
questions.guidance: Compare the inventory with the critical system list.

references.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography, August 2023
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Quantum-vulnerable algorithm identification
controls.objective: Every use of RSA, elliptic curve, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman for key establishment or signatures is identified and recorded as quantum-vulnerable.

evidence.description: List of quantum-vulnerable uses by system

questions.text: Has each use of RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, DH, and ECDH been identified and flagged as quantum-vulnerable, by system?
questions.guidance: Partial: identified for TLS only, not for code signing, VPN, SSH, or stored data.

questions.text: Number of critical systems that rely on quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms
questions.guidance: Count from the inventory.

references.source: NIST IR 8547 ipd, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
references.note: initial public draft; check for final version

controls.title: Data longevity and harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure
controls.objective: Each data class has a recorded confidentiality lifetime, and classes exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later collection are flagged.

evidence.description: Data classification with retention and confidentiality periods

questions.text: Does each data class have a recorded number of years it must stay confidential?
questions.guidance: Partial: retention periods exist but confidentiality lifetime is not stated.

questions.text: Number of data classes that must stay confidential for 10 years or more and travel over networks protected only by quantum-vulnerable key exchange
questions.guidance: Combine the data classification with the inventory of protocols used to transmit each class.

references.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography, August 2023
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Encryption of data at rest
controls.objective: Sensitive data at rest is encrypted with approved algorithms and managed keys.

evidence.description: Disk, database, and backup encryption settings

questions.text: Percentage of endpoints, servers, and backup stores holding sensitive data that use full-disk or storage encryption
questions.guidance: Use management console reports.

questions.text: Is AES with 256-bit keys used for data that must stay confidential for 10 years or more?
questions.guidance: Partial: AES-128 used. Target to confirm: AES-256 follows CNSA 2.0 for national security systems; confirm whether the client adopts it for commercial data.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Encryption of data in transit
controls.objective: Data in transit uses current protocol versions with strong cipher suites.

evidence.description: TLS scan of external and internal endpoints

questions.text: Number of endpoints that accept TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, SSL, or cipher suites without forward secrecy
questions.guidance: Use a TLS scanner on in-scope endpoints.

questions.text: Is TLS 1.3 enabled on externally facing services?
questions.guidance: TLS 1.3 is the version where hybrid post-quantum key exchange is being deployed. Partial: enabled on some externally facing services but not all.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Key and certificate management
controls.objective: Keys and certificates have owners, are stored in protected key stores, and are rotated and revoked under a defined process.

questions.text: Are private keys for critical services held in an HSM or managed key vault rather than in files on servers?
questions.guidance: Partial: some services.

questions.text: Number of certificates found expired or expiring within 30 days without a renewal ticket
questions.guidance: Use the certificate inventory or a scan.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Crypto agility
controls.objective: Algorithms and parameters are selected by configuration or central libraries so that they can be changed without code changes in each application.

questions.text: How are cryptographic algorithms selected in the organization's critical applications?

anchors.label: Hard-coded
anchors.description: Algorithms are hard-coded in each application.

anchors.label: Mixed
anchors.description: Some applications use configuration or a central library; others are hard-coded.

anchors.label: Configurable
anchors.description: All critical applications select algorithms by configuration or a central library.

anchors.label: Proven
anchors.description: Configurable, and an algorithm change has been carried out in at least one application in the last 24 months.

questions.guidance: Ask for an example of how a change of algorithm would be made.

references.source: NIST IR 8547 ipd, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
references.note: initial public draft; check for final version

controls.title: Vendor PQC roadmaps
controls.objective: Critical vendors have provided written plans for supporting ML-KEM, ML-DSA, or SLH-DSA, and these are tracked.

questions.text: Percentage of critical vendors using public-key cryptography that have provided a written PQC roadmap with dates
questions.guidance: Use the vendor tracker.

questions.text: Do new contracts for products that use public-key cryptography require support for FIPS 203, 204, or 205 by a stated date?
questions.guidance: Partial: requirement in some contracts.

references.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography, August 2023
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: PQC migration plan
controls.objective: A risk-prioritized roadmap with owners and dates moves systems to ML-KEM and ML-DSA or SLH-DSA, aligned to the NIST transition timeline.

questions.text: Is there a PQC migration roadmap with named owners and target dates, prioritized by data longevity and system criticality?
questions.guidance: Partial: roadmap without owners or dates.

questions.text: Do the roadmap's target dates finish moving critical systems off quantum-vulnerable algorithms by 2035, the disallowance date in the IR 8547 draft?
questions.guidance: Partial: target dates by 2035 exist for some critical systems but not all. Target to confirm: the IR 8547 draft dates (deprecate 2030, disallow 2035); check the current version of IR 8547.

questions.text: Does the target state name ML-KEM for key establishment and ML-DSA or SLH-DSA for signatures, with parameter sets chosen?
questions.guidance: Partial: algorithms named without parameter sets.

references.source: NIST IR 8547 ipd, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
references.note: initial public draft; check for final version
paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Hybrid deployment and PQC testing
controls.objective: Hybrid or post-quantum deployments are documented and tested for interoperability and performance using validated implementations.

evidence.description: Test reports and hybrid configuration records

questions.text: Has at least one PQC or hybrid (classical plus ML-KEM) configuration been tested for interoperability and performance, with results recorded?
questions.guidance: Partial: tested in a lab without recorded results.

questions.text: Where hybrid key establishment is deployed, is the combination and the plan to retire the classical part documented?
questions.guidance: Answer N/A if no hybrid is deployed. Partial: the hybrid combination is documented but there is no plan to retire the classical part.

questions.text: Are PQC implementations in use drawn from libraries or modules with NIST algorithm validation (CAVP) or FIPS 140-3 validation where required?
questions.guidance: Ask for certificate numbers. Partial: validated libraries or modules for some PQC implementations but not all, or validation is still in process.

references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container
